# dsh-github-oss-radar
A persistent DeepSeek Harness (dsh) bundle that gives every agent in a profile a standing GitHub-fir
st open-source check: on each new request the model extracts keywords, calls one budgeted `github_se
arch` tool, and lists the reusable repositories that genuinely fit, if any, before it answers.

- Package: `dsh-github-oss-radar` 0.1.0, MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/Otto883/dsh-github-oss

-radar
- ESM, zero runtime dependencies, verified on dsh `0.1.7-rc.2`
## Why this instead of a skill
- A skill runs only when the model decides to load it. This bundle installs a system-prompt policy i

nstead, so the check happens on every new request without a decision step.
- The policy is budgeted
on purpose: at most one `github_search` call per request, identical concurrent requests coalesced in

to one, and responses cached in memory for 10 minutes.
- The list is a starting point, not a substit
ute for the answer. The policy says the search must not delay the response and never replaces readin
g the user's own files, and a follow-up inside the same subject does not repeat the search.
## What it installs
Both parts are registered for every agent of the profile.
| Kind | Name | Effect |
| System-prompt section | `github-oss-radar:policy` | Added at order `1990`, just before the built-i
n web-search guidance. Tells the model to extract 1-4 English keywords from each new request, call `
github_search` once before answering, and list up to 5 (configurable) genuinely relevant repositorie
s as `owner/repo` (★ count) with one line on what each does and why it fits, plus the URL. When noth

ing is relevant it says so in one line. |
| Host tool | `github_search` | Searches `https://api.gith
ub.com/search/repositories` and returns a compact, model-readable list of repositories. |
The tool accepts these arguments:
| Argument | Type | Description |
| `keywords` | array of 1-4 strings | English technical keywords naming the technology, domain, or t
ask. Required unless `query` is given. Joined with spaces, so keywords are combined with AND semanti

cs. |
| `query` | string | Exact GitHub repository search query. Overrides `keywords` when present.

|
| `language` | string | Optional GitHub language filter, for example `Python` or `TypeScript`. |
|

`min_stars` | integer | Minimum star count. Defaults to the plugin setting (`minStars`). |
| `limit
` | integer, 1-10 | Number of repositories to return. Defaults to the plugin setting (`maxResults`).

|
| `sort` | `stars` or `updated` or `best-match` | Result ordering. Defaults to `stars`. |
The composed query is the keywords joined with spaces, plus `stars:>=N` when a minimum star count is
set, plus `language:X` when a language is set, plus `archived:false` unless `includeArchived` is on
. If the full keyword set matches no repository and no explicit `query` was given, the tool retries
once, broadened to the first keyword.

## Rate limits and tokens
Unauthenticated requests to the GitHub Search API are limited to 10 requests per minute. The bundle
is designed to stay inside that budget: at most one search per new request, identical concurrent req
uests coalesced into a single call, and responses cached in memory for 10 minutes (`cacheTtlMs`).
When GitHub does reject a search for rate limiting, the tool reports the reset time and suggests set
ting `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the policy tells the model to continue without the list rather than retrying.
A token is optional. The plugin reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` from the Host environment. The `t
okenEnv` key names the variable that is read (default `GITHUB_TOKEN`). An optional `token` config ke
y exists as well, but the environment variable is the recommended route. No token is required; witho
ut one, the anonymous 10 requests per minute limit applies.
## Requirements

- dsh `0.1.7-rc.2` (verified compatible).
- Node.js `22.19.0` or newer for the Host runtime; the plu

gin uses the global `fetch` and Node built-ins.
- No runtime dependencies.
